_README: THE STANDARD SYLLABUS TEMPLATE. Every course's syllabus gets normalized into this exact shape, no matter how the instructor wrote it. Fluff (Title IX, ADA, nondiscrimination, religious-accommodation, academic-integrity boilerplate, learning-outcome prose, motivational filler) is dropped - it is identical across every UVU course and changes no decision. Only decision-relevant facts survive. Rules for what counts as real vs fluff: courses/AGENT-PROMPT.md section B2. Never hand-edit a source syllabus; edit this file.

_schema.title: string

grading.components: [{ name, points, weight, note }] - weight is % of final grade
grading.scale: [{ grade, min }] - min % for that letter, descending

_schema.assessments: [{ name, covers, date, points, cumulative, format }]
_schema.policies: { attendance, late, makeup, retake, drop, materialsAllowed }
_schema.keyRules: [string] - the few facts that actually change how you study
_schema.conflicts: [string] - contradictions IN THE SOURCE. Never silently resolve one.
_schema.source: string - where this was normalized from

CHEM 1210.title: General Chemistry I

materials.note: learn-ai-DanielScott26.replit.app - homework 'progress questions' live inside the text and are graded
Must have logarithm, scientific notation and exponent capability. Permitted on quizzes and exams.
Provided during quizzes - do not buy one.

components.name: Attendance
components.note: First 3 absences cost 5 pts each; every absence after costs 10.

components.name: Homework
components.note: Progress questions inside the AcademiQ text.

components.name: Quizzes
components.note: ~25 quizzes at 8 pts. Timed. Due 30 min before class. Quiz title names the practice problems it covers.

components.name: Final exam
components.note: Comprehensive ACS standardized exam. Cannot be made up.

grading.curveNote: Exams mirror ACS standardized exams where the class average is expected to be 50%, so the scale is shifted down: 63% is a C, not a D. Do not read these cutoffs against a normal 90/80/70 scale.

assessments.name: Final (comprehensive)
assessments.format: ACS standardized, in class 1:00 PM. No makeup.

policies.attendance: Graded, 100 pts. First 3 absences -5 each, then -10 each. Instructor states 5 absences likely means a low grade, 10 likely means failing.
policies.makeup: The final exam cannot be made up. No makeup policy stated for midterms.
policies.retake: No retakes, but see 'drop' - later exams retroactively raise earlier ones.
policies.drop: Nothing is dropped. Instead: because exams are cumulative, improving on a later exam RETROACTIVELY raises your earlier exam scores when final grades are tallied.
policies.materialsAllowed: Calculator and blank scratch paper permitted. Periodic table provided. Quizzes are closed-note and must be done independently.

keyRules: Every exam is cumulative, and a later exam retroactively raises earlier ones. Early material never stops mattering - and a bad Exam 1 is recoverable.
The scale is curved: 63% is a C. Exams are built to an expected 50% class average.
The final is 25% of the grade, comprehensive, ACS-standardized, and cannot be made up. Dec 7, 1:00 PM.
Attendance is 9% of the grade and is scored by a penalty formula, not by showing up occasionally.
Quizzes are due 30 minutes BEFORE class, not at end of day. The quiz title names exactly which practice problems it covers.
conflicts: TWO different grade breakdowns appear in the same syllabus. The points table (Attendance 100 / Homework 50 / Quizzes 200 / Exams 475 / Final 275 = 1100) disagrees with a later section that lists Attendance 8%, Homework+Quizzes 19%, THREE midterms at 11% each (~45%), Final 28%. The points table is used here because it sums exactly to 1100 and matches the four-exam schedule; the later section appears to be stale text from a different section of the course.
'Exams (4 x 125)' is listed as 475 points, but 4 x 125 = 500. The 475 figure is used here because it is what makes the components total the stated 1100.
Prose says the final is 'worth 250 points'; the points table says 275. The table is used, for the same reason.
